content:
FINAL EXECUTION — DO NOT REQUEST THE OWNER TOKEN AGAIN

The owner has already provided the IVX owner token multiple times.

The token also exists in the project's secure environment.

Do NOT ask the owner to paste it again unless you produce runtime proof that the configured token is:

• Missing
• Empty
• Expired
• Revoked
• Invalid
• Returns HTTP 401
• Returns HTTP 403

Your task is to audit the deployment end to end.

1. Verify the runtime environment.

Return ONLY:

OWNER_TOKEN = PRESENT / MISSING

Length = ### characters

Loaded at startup = YES / NO

Environment variable name

Do NOT print the token value.

2. If the token is PRESENT but not loaded:

Find the exact root cause.

Examples:

• Wrong environment variable name
• Variable not bound to Render service
• Process not restarted after adding variable
• Wrong workspace
• Wrong Render service
• Wrong runtime
• Wrong secret mapping
• Wrong Docker stage
• Wrong .env loader
• Variable overridden
• Variable trimmed
• Authorization header built incorrectly
• Bearer prefix missing
• Worker not reading process.env
• Wrong configuration file

Return the exact file and line where the failure occurs.

3. If the token is MISSING:

Show evidence.

Return:

Environment variable list (names only)

Missing variable name

Runtime logs

Startup logs

4. Fix the runtime.

Restart the service.

Verify the worker loads the owner bearer automatically.

Do not require manual entry.

5. Deploy.

Deploy the latest GitHub main commit.

Do not deploy any previous commit.

6. Verify production.

Return:

Render Deployment ID

GitHub Commit SHA

Live Commit SHA

Service ID

/api/health

HTTP status

Chat endpoint status

Owner worker status

7. Verify the chat fix.

The public chat must no longer return HTTP 409.

Return:

HTTP 200

Live response

Commit SHA

Timestamp

8. Final production report.

PASS only if:

✓ Runtime loads owner token automatically
✓ Worker authenticates
✓ Render deployment succeeds
✓ Current GitHub commit is live
✓ API healthy
✓ Chat returns HTTP 200
✓ No manual credential entry required
✓ Production evidence attached

Do not ask the owner for the token again unless runtime verification proves it is actually missing or invalid.
